the bivariate spatial correlation measure is able to discover the top-k and top-k crime patterns and the visualization of the results provides a better understanding of criminal activities.

we introduce a bivariate correlation measure for crime analysis that is able to extract cross correlations from areal aggregated crime datasets, that can be extended into multivariate correlations, and that can visualize the resulting patterns.

we have developed a novel spatial bivariate correlation approach for discovering cross-correlation patterns between heterogeneous datasets and have demonstrated its applicability and usefulness with a real crime analysis case study.

the following questions: (i) What is the correlation of crime activities?
the development of a novel spatial correlation measure that allows for the discovery of cross correlations from heterogeneous data types.
the development and evaluation of a bivariate spatial cross correlation approach for criminal cross correlation mining and visualization.

the proposed bivariate approach is able to extract meaningful patterns that cannot be extracted using existing techniques.
the proposed approach is a promising tool to discover crime correlations in a spatially, temporally, and thematically heterogeneous environment.
the proposed approach is able to extract top-k and bottom k associative features and visualize the resulting crime patterns.

the proposed bivariate spatial correlation measure can be used to identify cross-correlated features from crime datasets.
the proposed approach can be used to discover crime correlations and can be used for crime analysis.

cross correlation mining can be a powerful technique to discover crime correlations and patterns.
the bivariate spatial correlation is an effective approach for discovering cross correlation in heterogeneous datasets.
